   "id": "e89f81f1",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "# Parallel (associative-scan) solvers\n",
    "\n",
    "The Riccati recursion in LQR is sequential: step $t$ needs step $t+1$. However, the recursion can\n",
    "be rewritten as an **associative** combination of per-step elements, which\n",
    "`jax.lax.associative_scan` evaluates in $O(\\log T)$ parallel depth (Särkkä & García-Fernández,\n",
    "2023). diffilqrax provides parallel counterparts of every solver:\n",
    "\n",
    "| sequential | parallel |\n",
    "|---|---|\n",
    "| `lqr.solve_lqr` | `plqr.solve_plqr` |\n",
    "| `ilqr.ilqr_solver` | `parallel_ilqr.pilqr_solver` |\n",
    "| `diff_lqr.dlqr` | `parallel_dlqr.pdlqr` |\n",
    "| `diff_ilqr.dilqr` | `parallel_dilqr.pdilqr` |\n",
    "\n",
    "The parallel versions take the same arguments and converge to the same solutions. This notebook\n",
    "checks that on a long-horizon iLQR problem and shows how run time scales with the horizon.\n",
    "\n",
    "The parallel solvers do more total work, so on a **CPU** you should not expect a speed-up; at\n",
    "best they roughly match the sequential solver. The benefit appears on a **GPU** with long\n",
    "horizons, where the sequential solver is limited by its $O(T)$ depth."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 1,
   "id": "00ecd3b6",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-14T22:41:27.642118Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-14T22:41:27.641821Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-14T22:41:28.278938Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-14T22:41:28.278341Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",

     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "import time as timer\n",
    "\n",
    "import jax\n",
    "import jax.numpy as jnp\n",
    "import jax.random as jr\n",
    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
    "\n",
    "from diffilqrax.ilqr import ilqr_solver\n",
    "from diffilqrax.parallel_ilqr import pilqr_solver, dynamics_defects\n",
    "from diffilqrax.diff_ilqr import dilqr\n",
    "from diffilqrax.parallel_dilqr import pdilqr\n",
    "from diffilqrax.typs import System, ModelDims, iLQRParams, Theta\n",
    "\n",
    "jax.config.update(\"jax_enable_x64\", True)\n",
    "print(\"device:\", jax.devices()[0])"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "e5101561",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## A long-horizon problem\n",
    "\n",
    "A stable tanh RNN, $x_{t+1} = \\tanh(U_h x_t + W_h u_t)$, tracks a slow sine wave in every state."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 2,
   "id": "4b600865",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-14T22:41:28.282832Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-14T22:41:28.282597Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-14T22:41:28.861235Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-14T22:41:28.860597Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "N, M = 8, 3\n",
    "k1, k2 = jr.split(jr.PRNGKey(0))\n",
    "theta = Theta(Uh=0.8 * jr.normal(k1, (N, N)) / jnp.sqrt(N), Wh=jr.normal(k2, (N, M)) / jnp.sqrt(N), sigma=0.0, Q=None)\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "def make_model(horizon):\n",
    "    def cost(t, x, u, th):\n",
    "        return jnp.sum((x - 0.5 * jnp.sin(t / 50.0)) ** 2) + 0.1 * jnp.sum(u**2)\n",
    "\n",
    "    def costf(x, th):\n",
    "        return jnp.sum(x**2)\n",
    "\n",
    "    def dynamics(t, x, u, th):\n",
    "        return jnp.tanh(th.Uh @ x + th.Wh @ u)\n",
    "\n",
    "    return System(cost, costf, dynamics, ModelDims(n=N, m=M, horizon=horizon, dt=0.1))\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "params = iLQRParams(x0=jnp.zeros(N), theta=theta)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "9200c22c",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Same solution\n",
    "\n",
    "`pilqr_solver` has two ways to roll out a candidate step:\n",
    "\n",
    "- `rollout=\"feedback\"` (default) runs the parallel Riccati scan, then a sequential non-linear\n",
    "  rollout under the feedback policy, exactly like `ilqr_solver`. Every iterate is a feasible\n",
    "  trajectory.\n",
    "- `rollout=\"parallel\"` uses **multiple shooting**. The states are also optimisation variables, the\n",
    "  dynamics defects $d_t = f(x_t, u_t) - x_{t+1}$ enter the local LQR, and the whole step is\n",
    "  computed with associative scans. Iterates are feasible only at convergence, so we report the\n",
    "  largest defect."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 3,
   "id": "ec3abdaf",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-14T22:41:28.864605Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-14T22:41:28.864372Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-14T22:41:58.620285Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-14T22:41:58.619475Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "ilqr             J = 745.6031498673\n",
      "pilqr feedback   J = 745.6031498673   max|ΔU| = 1.2e-15\n"
     ]
    },
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "pilqr parallel   J = 745.6031498673   max|ΔU| = 7.0e-13   max defect = 3.3e-16\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "T = 1000\n",
    "model = make_model(T)\n",
    "Us_init = jnp.zeros((T, M))\n",
    "\n",
    "(Xs, Us, _), J, _ = ilqr_solver(model, params, Us_init, max_iter=200)\n",
    "(Xf, Uf, _), Jf, _ = pilqr_solver(model, params, Us_init, max_iter=200, rollout=\"feedback\")\n",
    "(Xp, Up, _), Jp, _ = pilqr_solver(model, params, Us_init, max_iter=200, rollout=\"parallel\")\n",
    "\n",
    "print(f\"ilqr             J = {float(J):.10f}\")\n",
    "print(f\"pilqr feedback   J = {float(Jf):.10f}   max|ΔU| = {jnp.max(jnp.abs(Uf - Us)):.1e}\")\n",
    "print(f\"pilqr parallel   J = {float(Jp):.10f}   max|ΔU| = {jnp.max(jnp.abs(Up - Us)):.1e}   \"\n",
    "      f\"max defect = {jnp.max(jnp.abs(dynamics_defects(model, params, Xp, Up))):.1e}\")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 4,
   "id": "673b7f96",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-14T22:41:58.623605Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-14T22:41:58.623341Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-14T22:42:00.473076Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-14T22:42:00.472513Z"
    },

    ]
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",

       "<Figure size 900x450 with 2 Axes>"
      ]
     },

   ],
   "source": [
    "time = jnp.arange(T + 1)\n",
    "fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(9, 4.5), sharex=True, layout=\"constrained\")\n",
    "axes[0].plot(time, 0.5 * jnp.sin(time / 50.0), \"k\", lw=0.8, label=\"target\")\n",
    "for (X, U), style, label in [((Xs, Us), \"-\", \"ilqr\"), ((Xf, Uf), \"--\", \"pilqr feedback\"), ((Xp, Up), \":\", \"pilqr parallel\")]:\n",
    "    axes[0].plot(time, X[:, 0], style, label=label)\n",
    "    axes[1].plot(time[:-1], U[:, 0], style)\n",
    "axes[0].set(ylabel=\"$x_0$\")\n",
    "axes[1].set(ylabel=\"$u_0$\", xlabel=\"t\")\n",
    "axes[0].legend(ncol=4, fontsize=8);"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "b6d81305",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Gradients agree too\n",
    "\n",
    "`pdilqr` is the parallel counterpart of `dilqr`. Both the forward solve and the adjoint LQR in the\n",
    "reverse pass use associative scans."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 5,
   "id": "dc1f9eea",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-14T22:42:00.475802Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-14T22:42:00.475609Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-14T22:42:25.829062Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-14T22:42:25.828568Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "dL/dUh: relative difference 9.8e-15\n",
      "dL/dWh: relative difference 7.1e-15\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "Ts = 200\n",
    "model_s = make_model(Ts)\n",
    "U0 = jnp.zeros((Ts, M))\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "def loss(solver, th):\n",
    "    return jnp.sum(solver(model_s, iLQRParams(params.x0, th), U0, max_iter=200) ** 2)\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "g_seq = jax.grad(lambda th: loss(dilqr, th))(theta)\n",
    "g_par = jax.grad(lambda th: loss(pdilqr, th))(theta)\n",
    "for name in (\"Uh\", \"Wh\"):\n",
    "    a, b = getattr(g_par, name), getattr(g_seq, name)\n",
    "    print(f\"dL/d{name}: relative difference {jnp.linalg.norm(a - b) / jnp.linalg.norm(b):.1e}\")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "92d6b7b2",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Scaling with the horizon\n",
    "\n",
    "We time one jitted solve at several horizons. The absolute numbers depend on your hardware. On a\n",
    "CPU, all three scale linearly and take similar time. On a GPU, the `\"parallel\"` rollout should\n",
    "scale best."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 6,
   "id": "dbe0f994",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-14T22:42:25.831830Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-14T22:42:25.831644Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-14T22:44:05.648237Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-14T22:44:05.647467Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "def time_solver(solve, model, n_repeat=3):\n",
    "    Us0 = jnp.zeros((model.dims.horizon, M))\n",
    "    f = jax.jit(lambda p, u: solve(model, p, u, max_iter=200))\n",
    "    jax.block_until_ready(f(params, Us0))  # compile\n",
    "    start = timer.perf_counter()\n",
    "    for _ in range(n_repeat):\n",
    "        jax.block_until_ready(f(params, Us0))\n",
    "    return (timer.perf_counter() - start) / n_repeat\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "solvers = {\n",
    "    \"ilqr\": ilqr_solver,\n",
    "    \"pilqr feedback\": lambda m, p, u, **kw: pilqr_solver(m, p, u, rollout=\"feedback\", **kw),\n",
    "    \"pilqr parallel\": lambda m, p, u, **kw: pilqr_solver(m, p, u, rollout=\"parallel\", **kw),\n",
    "}\n",
    "horizons = [250, 500, 1000, 2000]\n",
    "timings = {name: [time_solver(s, make_model(h)) for h in horizons] for name, s in solvers.items()}"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 7,
   "id": "820e7827",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-14T22:44:05.651392Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-14T22:44:05.651150Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-14T22:44:06.058304Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-14T22:44:06.057586Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 500x350 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3.5), layout=\"constrained\")\n",
    "for name, ts in timings.items():\n",
    "    ax.loglog(horizons, ts, \"o-\", label=name)\n",
    "ax.set(xlabel=\"horizon T\", ylabel=\"wall time per solve (s)\", title=f\"device: {jax.devices()[0].platform}\")\n",
    "ax.legend();"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "77d3d7a3",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## How to adapt\n",
    "\n",
    "- **Switching solver:** replace `ilqr_solver` with `pilqr_solver` (or `dilqr` with `pdilqr`). The\n",
    "  model, parameters and initial inputs are unchanged.\n",
    "- **Choosing a rollout:** use `\"feedback\"` when you need every iterate to be feasible, for example\n",
    "  when stopping early. Use `\"parallel\"` for the most parallelism on a GPU.\n",
    "- **Non-convex costs:** `make_psd=\"R\"` or `\"full\"` projects the local problem to be convex, which\n",
    "  makes every scan element valid without regularisation retries.\n",
    "- **Gradient adjoint:** `pdilqr(..., adjoint=\"sequential\")` solves the reverse LQR sequentially.\n",
    "  This is useful for checking results or on a CPU.\n",
    "- **Benchmarking on a GPU:** install a CUDA build of JAX and re-run this notebook. For a script\n",
    "  version, see `examples/long_horizon.py` in the repository."
   ]
  }
